topic_title: What If The Entire Internet Disappeared For 24 Hours?
topic_angle: A chronological hour-by-hour breakdown of global infrastructure collapse: BGP table drops, DNS blackouts, power grid telemetry failures, air traffic rerouting, and cash transaction failure.
key_themes: Societal Reliance on Digital Time & Settlement

timeline_events.description: Global BGP keepalive timers expire. Every peering router drops adjacent routes. Ping replies cease worldwide.
Billions of smartphones repeatedly send reconnect handshakes, overwhelming radio tower control channels in a signaling storm.
Supermarkets, gas stations, and pharmacies experience POS terminal timeouts. Cash registers become islands.
Automated warehouse robotics and RFID tracking stop dispatching trucks. Container ports cannot match manifests.
SCADA systems on regional electrical grids lose remote telemetry and switch to autonomous local islanding mode.
FM/AM radio broadcasts, emergency sirens, and printed bulletin boards become the primary source of human communication.
Packet routing restores; the unprecedented thundering herd of 100 billion queued HTTP requests slams data centers.

technical_mechanisms.name: BGP Route Flapping & Convergence
technical_mechanisms.explanation: When thousands of network prefixes disappear, routers attempt to recalculate alternative paths, causing CPU saturation across core routing ASNs.

technical_mechanisms.name: DNS TTL Decay
technical_mechanisms.explanation: Cached domain records begin to expire sequentially. High-traffic CDNs with 60-second TTLs fail first; slow enterprise domains survive longer.

technical_mechanisms.name: Thundering Herd Problem on Recovery
technical_mechanisms.explanation: The moment connectivity returns, millions of IoT sensors, phones, and automated workers send simultaneous retries, triggering secondary outages.

verified_facts.claim: Submarine fiber-optic cables carry over 99% of all intercontinental internet traffic, spanning over 1.4 million kilometers.
verified_facts.notes: Verified against ITU-T optical transport recommendations.

verified_facts.claim: BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) routing tables hold over 950,000 active IPv4 routes and over 200,000 IPv6 routes; a global drop triggers instantaneous packet routing failure.
verified_facts.primary_source: CIDR Report / RIPE NCC Routing Information Service
verified_facts.notes: RFC 4271 defines BGP-4 protocol behavior upon keepalive timeout (default 90 seconds).

verified_facts.claim: DNS Root Servers (A through M) are operated by 12 independent organizations across over 1,500 anycast nodes worldwide.
verified_facts.notes: TTL caching allows existing domain names to resolve for 1-24 hours depending on zone TTL.

verified_facts.claim: Global interbank settlement systems like Fedwire and SWIFT process over $5 trillion daily; an outage freezes clearing and debit/credit authorizations worldwide.
verified_facts.primary_source: Federal Reserve Financial Services Data / Bank for International Settlements (BIS)
verified_facts.notes: ATMs and Point-of-Sale terminals fall back to offline floors or fail outright.

verified_facts.claim: Modern cellular base stations rely on fiber backhaul (PTP / IEEE 1588v2 Precision Time Protocol) for phase synchronization; without backhaul, cell towers drop user sessions within minutes.
verified_facts.notes: Even local tower-to-phone RF fails to route without upstream EPC/5GC core.

verified_facts.claim: Air Traffic Control systems use separate VHF radio voice channels, but flight planning, radar data feeds, and NOTAM updates depend on the aeronautical telecommunications network.
verified_facts.primary_source: FAA / Eurocontrol Aeronautical Information Management Architecture
verified_facts.notes: Planes in the air land safely via radio; grounded planes cannot take off due to flight plan filing lockouts.
